stories.title: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 31
stories.summary: At least 30 people have been killed after a mound of rubbish at a major waste site collapsed onto nearby homes in Guinea's capital Conakry, the government has said. Another 22 people were injured, including six seriously, in the city's Dar-es-Salam area. "Significant" resources and personnel - including the military - were deployed to search for survivors after the collapse at about 02:00 local time following heavy rain overnight, the government added in a statement. One woman told local media her five children had died in the disaster. There are fears that the death toll will rise further. Rescuers were later seen using excavators to comb through a mountain of scattered rubbish at the site as local residents gathered nearby. Guinea's Prime Minister Mamadou Oury Bah visited the scene to assess the situation and oversee the search efforts. Neighbourhood leader Lancine Sylla had earlier told the AFP news agency that he feared there would be a heavy death toll. "We have pulled out 18 bodies that were taken to the morgue," he said. Another landslide at the site killed 10 people in 2017.

stories.title: Kiev loses nearly 9,900 soldiers, mercenaries over week of fighting — expert
stories.summary: LUGANSK, August 24. The Ukrainian armed forces’ losses in killed and wounded, including foreign mercenaries, totaled 9,900 personnel over the past week, military expert. Andrey Marochko reported. He stated that fighters of Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted the heaviest losses on the enemy. "The enemy’s combat and irrecoverable losses for the week totaled about 9,850 militants and mercenaries, which is 265 more than in the previous reporting period. The greatest losses in manpower were inflicted on Ukrainian armed formations in the area of responsibility of the Battlegroup East, which operates in the Dnepropetrovsk and Zaporozhye Regions," he wrote on his VKontakte page after analyzing data released by the Russian Defense Ministry. Marochko added that over the course of the week, the Russian military also destroyed a Ukrainian MiG-29 fighter aircraft, 8,477 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), two uncrewed boats, 12 marine vessels, three tanks, a Vampire multiple rocket launcher, three Grad multiple rocket launchers, 52 field artillery weapons, 46 electronic warfare and counter-battery stations, as well as more than 600 various enemy combat vehicles.

stories.title: Iran warns of 'consequences' for countries joining US economic sanctions
stories.summary: Iran warns of 'consequences' for countries joining US economic sanctions The Iranian Foreign Ministry warned on Monday that there would be "consequences" for countries joining the US campaign of economic pressure against the Islamic Republic. "The necessary warnings have certainly been issued, as any complicity with America in implementing its aggressive actions against Iran will undoubtedly have consequences," ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said during a weekly press conference. His comments come ahead of Washington's expected announcement later on Monday of new measures to isolate the Iranian economy.

stories.title: ‘Cookies’ made from plastic may be on the menu for future astronauts
stories.summary: Nasa-funded project uses yeasts to recycle plastics and other waste into food shaped into biscuits by 3D printers Cookies produced from upcycled plastic may sound like something straight out of a dystopian sci-fi plot. But researchers say that they have succeeded in creating such a product as part of a Nasa-funded project aimed at feeding astronauts on future space missions. The technology uses specially designed yeasts to transform plastics and agricultural waste into edible proteins, fats and flavourings. The resulting slurry is pased through a 3D printer to create a disc-shaped “cookie”. Continue reading...
